title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Raktamukha the monkey
cast.description: Clever, cheerful young monkey, generous and quick-thinking

cast.name: Karalamukha the crocodile
cast.description: Slow, foolish, guilt-ridden crocodile, adult male

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Sanskrit tradition. It is from the Panchatantra, the ancient book of fables attributed to Vishnu Sharma. It is called... The Monkey and the Crocodile.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the bank of a wide river stood a rose-apple tree, and in it lived a monkey named Raktamukha.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One day a crocodile named Karalamukha crawled out of the water to rest in its shade. The monkey, being a good host, threw him some of the sweet fruit.

lines.speaker: monkey
lines.text: [cheerful] Here, friend! Try these. Sweetest rose-apples on the whole river!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] The crocodile came back the next day, and the next, and the two became fast friends. He always took some fruit home to his wife.

lines.speaker: wife
lines.text: [slow, scheming] If the fruit is so sweet... how much sweeter must be the heart of a monkey who eats it every day? Bring me that heart. Or I will not eat, or speak to you, ever again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crocodile was torn. But in the end, he went to the tree.

lines.speaker: crocodile
lines.text: [nervous] My friend... my wife wants to thank you. Come to dinner! Climb on my back, I'll carry you across.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The monkey happily agreed. But in the middle of the river, where the water was deepest, the crocodile felt guilty... and confessed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [tense] The monkey's blood ran cold. But his voice stayed calm.

lines.speaker: monkey
lines.text: [casually] Oh, my friend, why didn't you say so before? We monkeys keep our hearts safe in the hollow of the tree when we travel. Take me back, and I'll fetch it for her gladly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [amused] The foolish crocodile turned around. The moment they reached the bank, the monkey leapt into the highest branches.

lines.speaker: monkey
lines.text: [laughing, then firm] Fool! Who can take his heart out of his body? Go home. Our friendship is over. Someone who betrays a friend once will do it again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] The Panchatantra teaches that presence of mind is worth more than strength, and that trust once broken is hard to mend. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
